title: Republic of San Marino
capsule: San Marino claims the oldest continuous republican constitution in the world, tracing its origins to a Christian community founded on Monte Titano by the stonemason Marinus of Rab around 301 CE and its formal communal government to the 13th century. During the Napoleonic period (1797–1815) the republic successfully preserved its independence: Napoleon explicitly guaranteed its sovereignty in 1797 and declined to absorb it, reportedly expressing admiration for a small state that embodied republican principles. The Grand and General Council, San Marino's parliament, continued to function without interruption, and the Congress of Vienna (1815) reaffirmed its status as a sovereign enclave within the newly reconstituted Italian peninsula.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. San Marino's territory of 61 km² on Monte Titano is precisely delimited and has been unchanged since 1463; historical sovereignty is well documented in Italian and papal records.
